attempts.summary: Created inventory-worker as an OpenRC-managed service on node1 (Alpine 3.23). The worker is a long-running shell loop (/usr/local/bin/inventory-worker.sh) that writes periodic snapshots to /var/lib/inventory/state.json and worker.log. It is confined via bubblewrap (bwrap --unshare-all with a read-only bind of / and a read-write bind only of /var/lib/inventory) launched through setpriv, which drops to the dedicated non-root 'inventory' user (uid 103/gid 104) and sets --no-new-privs before exec'ing bwrap (which itself also enforces NoNewPrivs). The service is registered via /etc/init.d/inventory-worker using the supervise-daemon supervisor (avoids the double-fork/die-with-parent race seen with start-stop-daemon+command_background) and is enabled in the default runlevel. Verified pre- and post-restart that the running process has uid/gid 103/104, NoNewPrivs:1, root mounted read-only, and only /var/lib/inventory mounted read-write, and that writes outside that directory are rejected (Permission denied / Read-only file system) while writes inside succeed. Completed the mandatory single-node restart: captured boot_id 9eff3fed... and live service/write state, issued a native `reboot`, polled until the node returned with a new boot_id faa097b3... and near-zero uptime, and confirmed the service auto-started on boot and resumed writing new iterations with identical confinement properties.
